title: Research note: sharp off-target proper-star puncture threshold
head: 80431a74c31e807581f5c2258c87abe2084caacd
body:
PR669 proves the sharp puncture threshold for target-local stars and explicitly leaves punctured decoders using arbitrary off-target stars open. This **research note / scoped negative result** closes that larger scalar class: for every power-of-two k >= 2 and p >= k, decoding one retained target requires exactly **2(p-k)+1** deleted ports. **No new kappa or paid supplier is claimed.**

The written elementary proof establishes the stronger identity d(C_{p,k}) = 2(p-k+1) for the global degree-<k star evaluation code, including the empty star, for every k >= 2. It uses generalized-cube parity, an even-face lemma and restriction induction. At a power-of-two k, permitted target overlap-class corrections add no functions to that code. The attaining witness uses one nonempty (k-1)-star.

A ten-star p=5,k=4 example reaches the same threshold while all 16 target intersection cells survive. Thus PR669's **minimum threshold** extends globally, while its **local cell feasibility criterion** does not. Exact elimination checks local infeasibility for this example.

Changes are limited to research/global-star-puncture/ and one scoped workflow. The accepted conditional kappa remains 51110230636731/31250000000000000; selected-result, existing suppliers, generators and upstream/ are unchanged.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/global-star-puncture/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_GLOBAL_STAR_PUNCTURE: sharp deletion thresholds 3/5; 2 independent F2 engines; 960 correction rows; 12 negative controls`.

The complete deterministic receipt is compared on every run. A packed row-space quotient and a separately written list-RREF/nullspace implementation agree on 80/240-port domains, ranks 65/155 and distances 4/6. All 28,680 pair syndromes in the second domain are distinct. Coverage also includes all 38,344 codewords in seven small domains, exhaustive even-face support checks in dimensions 1–4, valid generalized-face cubes, and a non-power-of-two positive escape control. Finite replay supports the written proof; it is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

### Validation and limits

- Python 3.13.5 on Windows: normal and isolated optimized exact replays pass.
- Four harness tests pass: relocated minimal replay/export, corrupted receipt rejection with output preserved, changed contextual source rejection, and changed source-pin rejection.
- Separate AI proof/code review and an independent enumeration of all 131,072 local coefficient assignments corroborate the off-target example.
- Selected-record/source integrity and staged whitespace checks pass; the final checkout is clean.
- Scoped hosted Linux verification **passed on Python 3.11 and 3.13** at the submitted head: [fork run 38348453202](https://github.com/lukemansoor/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38348453202). Both jobs passed the exact receipt, four failure-detection tests, selected-result integrity and clean-checkout check. Upstream PR-triggered workflows await maintainer approval (`action_required`).
- Full make verify and frontier626-verify were not repeated for this isolated additive research package.

The theorem concerns one specified retained target, arbitrary global proper-star coefficients and fixed coefficients within each overlap class. Simultaneous all-target delivery, paid total preparation, dirty restoration, legal reader frames, hosting, recursive costs and analytic transfer remain separate obligations. Degree-k stars, source-dependent overlap corrections, nonlinear mechanisms and other geometries are outside scope.
